thread:
marta: quick RFC follow-up: calibration anchorpoints for mixed FP8/INT8 pipeline. TL;DR — store 3 anchors per layer (warm / steady / tail) to pick per-slice scale & drive fallback hysteresis. Link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/calib-anchorpoints :eyes:
noah: high-level 👍. main worry: swapping precision mid-kv-cache could break kernel-level shape expectations. we need a compatibility shim or version tag on cached tensors. :thinking:
sam: ops note — 3 anchors/layer increases model metadata size. ballpark: ~3 * 8 bytes * #layers for float64 scales, but we store float32 or int16 compressed -> much smaller. still want an estimate for large LLaMA-like models. also need telemetry events for anchor transitions for cost SLOs.
irene: runtime implications: prefer embedding anchors into the quant-profile proto so the planner can make atomic roll decisions. example config snippet to discuss:
```
calibration:
  anchors:
    - warm: {scale: 0.012, stat: "mean_abs"}
    - steady: {scale: 0.008, stat: "max_abs"}
    - tail: {scale: 0.004, stat: "q95_abs"}
  hysteresis: 2   # number of token windows before switching back
  quality_threshold: 0.02 # relative degscore allowed
```
irene: also thinking per-slice vs per-head: per-slice cheaper but per-head better quality. prefer per-slice default with opt-in per-head per-layer for heavy customers.
devon: runtime followups: two things — 1) shape-tagging for kv cache (add uint8 precision tag + version). 2) fast-path kernels need a guarantee that quantized layout is identical across precision transitions or we copy+recast. copy+recast cost may kill latency SLOs for short responses.
noah: +1 on a precision tag. if we add versioning we can lazily compact cache on transitions. also consider a small padding strategy so int8->4bit kernels can read same buffer with an offset.
sam: ops / infra: telemetry impact — emit events: anchor_selected(layer=?, anchor=warm|steady|tail, reason=latency|quality|cost). we can roll this into the Console as a per-model heatmap. frequency should be sampled (1%) to control ingestion.
marta: question for runtime folks: will adding anchor points require runtime to keep multiple quantized copies of the same weight (for each anchor) or can we recompute on the fly from a stored scale?
devon: we can store base fp16 weights + small per-anchor scale tables and quantize on the fly for infrequent transitions. for hot path we should pre-quantize two likely anchors (active + candidate) and keep them resident. memory tradeoff: extra ~model_size * 1/4 per prequantized copy (very rough).
irene: ops policy suggestion: default behavior = prequantize steady+warm for dedicated customers, lazy for hosted. include a customer override: quant.anchors.prewarm=true/false.
sam: security/compliance note: ensure KMS/HSM keys unaffected by extra metadata; no PII in anchors obviously.
marta: perf experiment ask: can eng-runtime pick 5 representative layers and simulate anchor transitions with 95th percentile latency target? will pair with ops to run a microcanary.
noah: i can add a synthetic replay harness for that. will push a branch with a trimmed model and the anchor toggles.
opsbot: deploy-bot: canary job started for branch `anchorpoints/sim-harness` — job id 54678 — https://ci.redwood/54678 :rocket:
devon: one more operational edge: when rolling model versions, anchors should be treated as first-class versioned artifacts. if a rollback occurs, keep anchor history to avoid stale auto-selection.
marta: agreed. we'll add a `anchors.v` field in model manifest. next steps: (1) devon/noah — propose proto change for quant-profile w/ anchors, (2) sam/ops — estimate telemetry+storage cost, (3) irene/runtime — spike prequantize vs on-the-fly and report perf numbers. will sync Thursday 11am. :calendar: 
noah: noted. I'll add preliminary numbers by EOD tomorrow.
sam: will scope telemetry estimate, sampling plan.
irene: will do spike, may need extra GPU for sims.
devon: will draft proto and push a short RFC patch.
marta: thanks all — keeping this lightweight. if anyone sees a blocker for the scheduling ping me. :thumbsup:
